table determination_gates
CREATE TABLE "determination_gates" (
    gate_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    parameter_id        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),
    -- The lens the finding applies to, NULL meaning every lens on this parameter. Not an FK set like
    -- specifications' four, because a gate is raised against a parameter by an audit that may not know which cells
    -- exist yet. A gate that names several lens columns applies to a cell that carries ALL of them.
    identity_code       TEXT REFERENCES "base_taxonomy_identity"(identity_code),
    icf_code            TEXT REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code),
    needs_code          TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code),
    medical_code        TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code),
    verdict             TEXT NOT NULL
                        CHECK (verdict IN ('UNLINKED', 'MISLINKED',
                                           'UNDER-CONSERVATIVE', 'CONTRADICTS', 'QUESTION')),
    -- The ladder-inversion guard: how strong the thing raising the gate actually is. A QUESTION has no such
    -- thing and carries NULL in all three trigger columns; every other verdict states them.
    trigger_ref_id      TEXT REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
    trigger_tier        INTEGER CHECK (trigger_tier BETWEEN 1 AND 6),
    trigger_evidence_type TEXT,
    detail              TEXT NOT NULL,
    raised_at           TEXT NOT NULL,
    raised_by_session   TEXT NOT NULL,
    resolved_at         TEXT,
    resolved_by_session TEXT,

    CHECK ((resolved_at IS NULL AND resolved_by_session IS NULL
            AND resolution_rationale IS NULL)
        OR (resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND resolved_by_session IS NOT NULL
            AND resolution_rationale IS NOT NULL)),
    CHECK ((verdict = 'QUESTION'
            AND trigger_tier IS NULL AND trigger_evidence_type IS NULL AND trigger_ref_id IS NULL)
        OR (verdict <> 'QUESTION'
            AND trigger_tier IS NOT NULL AND trigger_evidence_type IS NOT NULL))
)

def main():
    global SESSION, STAMP
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Determine one cell: a parameter under one or more lenses.",
        epilog="--db IS WRITTEN, NOT ONLY READ. The engine gathers the cell's evidence "
               "from it and INSERTs the determination -- plus any gap and convergence "
               "row -- straight back into it, committing before it exits. --emit-sql is "
               "a replayable COPY of those same inserts, not the only place they land: "
               "emit_batch_sql.py captures them from the scratch DB, so applying the "
               "artifact AS WELL double-inserts. Two consequences before you run: a --db "
               "that has been run against is no longer pristine, and a re-run for the "
               "same cell is refused by the row-identity index; and comparing two runs "
               "for determinism means two fresh copies, not one DB run twice. The "
               "canonical DB is refused outright.")
    ap.add_argument("--db", required=True,
                    help="scratch DB, READ for the evidence and WRITTEN with the "
                         "determination (NEVER data/guidebook.db)")
    ap.add_argument("--emit-sql", required=True,
                    help="path for the replayable SQL copy of the rows this run also "
                         "commits into --db")
    ap.add_argument("--parameter-id", dest="parameter_id", type=int, required=True,
                    help="base_parameters.parameter_id — THE SUBJECT (owner 2026-08-26)")
    # NO LONGER "the slug to gather from" -- B4c gathers by parameter_id. This is the
    # topic the determination is being RECORDED under: it lands in the report and in
    # the gap description's context, and it is required so a determination cannot be
    # made without saying which piece of work it belongs to.
    ap.add_argument("--slug", required=True,
                    help="the topic this determination is recorded under. It does NOT "
                         "select evidence -- sources are gathered by the extractions "
                         "they hold for --parameter-id whose live lens links carry every "
                         "lens code the cell states.")
    ap.add_argument("--identity", help="base_taxonomy_identity.identity_code")
    ap.add_argument("--icf", help="base_icf.icf_code — a real ICF b/d code")
    ap.add_argument("--needs", help="access_needs.need_code")
    ap.add_argument("--medical", help="base_taxonomy_medical.medical_code")
    ap.add_argument("--note", default="", help="why this cell is being determined")
    ap.add_argument("--session", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--stamp", required=True,
                    help="fixed timestamp, e.g. '2026-09-09 00:00:00'. An INPUT, never "
                         "now(): the engine run twice must be byte-identical.")
    ap.add_argument("--report-json", default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if os.path.abspath(args.db) == os.path.abspath(os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "data", "guidebook.db")):
        sys.exit("REFUSING: this engine never writes the canonical DB (owner-gated).")
    # The DB holds the bare session stem; the pointer form carries `.md` (CLAUDE.md section 7), and
    # a wrong form scopes a gate to nothing. A stamp is stored verbatim, so it is refused unless it
    # has the shape every live created_at has: dbcore.now() is 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM', and the engine's
    # own examples add seconds. Both refusals precede every write.
    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}(:\d{2})?", args.stamp):
        print(f"REFUSING: --stamp {args.stamp!r} is not 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' or 'YYYY-MM-DD "

#: Tables holding a parameter_id that merge-parameter deliberately does NOT re-point,

#: found from the live schema (PRAGMA foreign_key_list) and re-pointed, so a table added
#: later is moved by default and can only stay behind by being argued in here -- the
#: burden-of-proof shape dbcore.NOT_CAPTURED uses for the capture set (CLAUDE.md rule 8).
_MERGE_KEEPS_HISTORY = {
    "specifications": (
        "a determination is computed ON its parameter, and its derivation_sha hashes the "
        "parameter_id. merge-parameter refuses while either parameter has a LIVE one, so "
        "what remains is retired history, which stays on the parameter it was computed for "
        "rather than claiming a subject it never had"),
    "determination_gates": (
        "a gate is raised against a parameter; merge-parameter refuses while either "
        "parameter has an OPEN gate, so what remains is resolved history and stays where "
        "it was raised"),
}

#: The prior-version item-code shape CLAUDE.md section 7 warns every grep meets
#: (`E-08 Corridor Clear Width ...`). The owner's D3 guard is "Screen, then you approve",
#: and the screen named it: no old item code in a minted name.
_ITEM_CODE = re.compile(r"\b[A-Z]-[0-9]{2}\b")



def _parameter_row(conn, parameter_id, verb: str):
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT p.parameter_id, p.term_id, p.status, p.merged_into, p.notes, "
        "t.canonical_en FROM base_parameters p JOIN terms t ON t.term_id = p.term_id "
        "WHERE p.parameter_id = ?", (parameter_id,)).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise Refusal(f"{verb}: parameter_id {parameter_id}: no such parameter.")
    return row


def _refuse_live_work(conn, parameter_id, verb: str):
    """Refuse while a LIVE determination or an OPEN determination gate stands on it.

    A retirement or a merge changes what the parameter IS. A live determination was
    computed on it and would silently become a determination of a folded or abandoned
    subject; an open gate is a question about it that nobody could then answer. Retired
    determinations and resolved gates are history and do not block.
    """
    live = [r[0] for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT specification_id FROM specifications WHERE parameter_id = ? "
        "AND retired_at IS NULL ORDER BY 1", (parameter_id,))]
    if live:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{verb}: parameter {parameter_id} has LIVE determination(s) {live}. A "
            f"determination was computed on this parameter, and changing what the "
            f"parameter is would re-point it at a subject it was not computed for. Retire "
            f"each first (db.py retire-specification --specification-id N --reason ...), "
            f"then re-run this. Nothing was written.")
    gates = [r[0] for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT gate_id FROM determination_gates WHERE parameter_id = ? "
        "AND resolved_at IS NULL ORDER BY 1", (parameter_id,))]
    if gates:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{verb}: parameter {parameter_id} has OPEN determination gate(s) {gates}. "
            f"Resolve each with its rationale first (db.py resolve-determination-gate "
            f"--gate-id N --rationale ...): an open gate is a question about this "
            f"parameter that nobody could answer once it is retired or merged. Nothing was "
            f"written.")


def _updated(conn, table: str, session: str, stamp: str) -> dict:
    """The updated_* columns this table actually has, set to one stamp."""
    have = set(dbcore.columns(conn, table))
    return {k: v for k, v in (("updated_at", stamp), ("updated_by_session", session))
            if k in have}

## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms

The language–jurisdiction pairs and the identity registry can be changed only by hand-written SQL, which bypasses every refusal; they are also outside the captured set, so a change would not reach a migration.

**Evidence command** (run from the repository root, after the set-up block so that `$SCRATCH` exists; it reads the canonical database read-only or works on a copy):

```
python3 -I -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import dbcore;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(sorted({r[0] for r in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table'\")}-set(dbcore.writable_tables(c))))"
```

**Expected output today:** The list includes `lang_jur_map` and `base_taxonomy_identity`. It also prints other tables (read 2026-11-13: twelve more, among them `data_migrations` and `sqlite_sequence`, which `dbcore.NOT_CAPTURED` excludes by design); they are not this task's. Save the output (`> "$SCRATCH/evidence-before.txt"`). **After the change** the same command must print the same list with exactly those two names removed: the command prints one line, so `diff "$SCRATCH/evidence-before.txt" "$SCRATCH/evidence-after.txt"` shows that line changed, and the only names missing from the new line are those two.

If the output differs, the ground has moved: stop (section 9). Ids that appear in this command are probes read on 2026-11-12; where the command derives an id by query, that is deliberate, and a test you write must do the same (section 6).

## 4. The change

Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect.

1. **Four verbs in `scripts/db.py`, two per table,** each with the refusals that are its value. (This item said "two verbs only" and then listed four operations; the pilot built four, and the readers need all four.) The history of the requirement: an identity code added with an optional `--parent` (the existing `parent_code` column; T-102 needs it: the device decomposition of the owner's OD-14 answer makes `MOB` a parent) and an amend of its display name with the replaced value printed; [added 2026-11-12, OI-13 fold] the amend also takes `--description` and `--category`, because the names and descriptions of `LLD` and `UPL` are proposals the owner confirms after they are written (T-102, T-116), so correcting one must be one verb call, not a migration by hand. Add no history or provenance column (no reader yet: `T-102-design.md` section 12, H).
   - **Chosen (pilot 2026-11-13, corrected at the fold): one approval pointer for all four verbs, `--approval-ref`,** the full text of a dated `## ` heading of `references/project-standards.md` found exactly once (`dbcore.ledger_heading_count`; a leading `## ` is stripped). Reason: it is the shape `db.py` already uses for an owner's approval of a base-vocabulary entry (`mint-term-from-catalogue --approval-ref`, re-read by `validate_parameters` P2) and the one T-024's `add-jurisdiction` takes for the same kind of act (admitting a base code), so one family of base admissions has one pointer. The readers name an entry, not a sentence (T-102: "the fifth-set entry"; T-116: "the eighth-set entry"; T-101: the answer to OD-04), and an entry is named once by its heading, whereas a short quote is often not unique (`grep -c -F 'Owner answers 2026-11-12 (fifth set)' references/project-standards.md` printed 2 on 2026-11-13, while that entry's full heading is found once). The other two pointer shapes in `db.py` belong to other acts: `--ruling-quote` (`rename-term`, where the owner's words must contain the new name, so the words are the warrant) and `--decision-ref` (`revoke-declination`, a DR or a quote). This replaces the `--ledger-pointer` (a quote, `require_ledger_quote_once`) that this file and `T-102-design.md` section 9 proposed and that the pilot built; the requirement (a pointer to exactly one owner entry) is unchanged. **Accepted limitation**, as for `mint-term-from-catalogue` and `add-jurisdiction`: the pointer proves that a unique dated entry exists, not that it approves this act; the operator answers for the match. The pointer is checked and printed in the result (`approval_ref`) and is not stored: neither table has a column for it, and nothing would read one (CLAUDE.md §8). The research pull request that calls the verbs names it in its migration summary.
   - **Why every verb takes it.** Which language and jurisdiction pairs are researched is jurisdiction scope, and the identity codes are the population taxonomy; both are owner sign-off (CLAUDE.md §8). No verb here writes without an owner entry to point at, and this task decides no scope and no code: it writes no row. A language new to the map is admitted only through `add-lang-jur-pair` with such an entry (the existing `log-search` refusal already says "a language is added there, not at the search"); the result reports it as `new_language: true`.
   - **Chosen (pilot 2026-11-13, corrected at the fold): one helper, `dbcore.require_approval_heading(ref, subject) -> str`,** returning the heading with a leading `## ` stripped, or raising `Refusal` with `<subject>: --approval-ref <ref> carries no date …` or `… is the heading of <n> ledger entries; it must be exactly one …`. The four verbs call it, and the inline copies of the same check in `mint_term_from_catalogue` and T-024's `add_jurisdiction` are replaced by a call to it (locate each with `grep -n 'ledger_heading_count' scripts/db.py`). Keep the words "no date" and "exactly one" in the messages, and call the helper at the point where each verb ran its inline check: `test_scan_contract` M05, M05b, M05c and M05d match on those words (M05c and M05d swap `dbcore.LEDGER_PATH` for a fixture file, so the helper must read `LEDGER_PATH` at call time, as `ledger_heading_count` already does), and T-024's refusal cases match on its message. Reason: six verbs, one check, one home; it makes two copies deletable.
   - **Chosen (pilot 2026-11-13): the verbs.** Each refusal prints `REFUSING:` and writes nothing. Every vocabulary is read from the column's CHECK (`choices=dbcore.schema_choices(...)` for argparse and `dbcore.check_declared` in the function; rule 8), never typed. Each takes `--session` and `--dry-run`. Required flags are `required=True` in argparse, as in every other verb: a missing flag is an argparse usage error (exit 2), not a refusal, and a refusal is what a present but wrong value meets (test them that way, section 6).
     - (a) `add-lang-jur-pair --language L --jurisdiction J --role R [--notes N] --approval-ref H --session S [--dry-run]`: INSERTs one `lang_jur_map` row, `scope_status` NULL (owed), `created_at` and `created_by_session` stamped. Refuses: a language blank or not upper case; a jurisdiction `dbcore.check_jurisdiction` refuses (admit it with `add-jurisdiction` first); a role outside the CHECK; a pair already held (a held pair's role is never rewritten here); an approval-ref the helper refuses. Result: `language`, `jurisdiction`, `role`, `new_language`, `approval_ref`. Reader: T-047 (AT-104 adds a pair by verb). **It is also what puts `lang_jur_map` in the captured set:** `dbcore._writer_tables()` derives the set from `INSERT INTO` text in `scripts/db.py` and `scripts/assess/assess_cell.py` only, so a table written only by UPDATE is not captured, and without this INSERT the UPDATEs of T-101's scope fill would never reach a migration.
     - (b) `set-pair-scope --language L --jurisdiction J --scope-status V --approval-ref H --session S [--dry-run]`: UPDATEs `scope_status` of one held pair. Refuses: a pair not held; a value outside the CHECK (NULL cannot be set back, and nothing needs it); the value the pair already has; an approval-ref the helper refuses. It does not check the jurisdiction (section 2). Result: `language`, `jurisdiction`, `scope_status`, `scope_status_was`, `approval_ref`. No `--reason`: the approval entry is the warrant, and no column would hold a reason. Reader: T-101 (one call per pair, each with the heading of the entry that records the answer to OD-04).
     - (c) `add-identity --code C --display-name N --category K --description D [--parent P] --approval-ref H --session S [--dry-run]`: INSERTs one `base_taxonomy_identity` row; `status` and `is_compound` take their column defaults; `created_at` and `updated_at` stamped (the table has no session column). Refuses: a code blank, not upper case or containing a space; a code already held, whatever its status; a blank display name or description; a category outside the CHECK; a `--parent` that is not a held `active` code; an approval-ref the helper refuses. Result: `identity_code`, `parent_code`, `approval_ref`. Readers: T-102 (the children, `--parent MOB`), T-116 (`UPL`, no parent).
     - (d) `amend-identity --code C [--display-name N] [--description D] [--category K] --approval-ref H --reason R --session S [--dry-run]`: UPDATEs the given fields and `updated_at` of a held code; never the code, the parent or the status (retiring is T-054's `retire-identity`). Refuses: no field given; a given value blank; a category outside the CHECK; a code not held; a blank `--reason` (`dbcore.require_reason`); an approval-ref the helper refuses. A field equal to its held value is not rewritten; when every given field is unchanged nothing is written and the result says `changed: false`. Result: `identity_code`, `changed`, `replaced` (each changed field with its old value), `now`, `reason`, `approval_ref`. `--reason` is kept because `T-102-design.md` section 9 fixes it and the amend verbs of `db.py` take one; it is printed, not stored. Readers: T-102 (`MOB`'s display name), T-116 (`UPL`, if the owner answers otherwise).
   - No migration, no new column, and no edit to `dbcore.writable_tables` or `NOT_CAPTURED`: the captured set gains both tables from the two INSERTs (confirm by the evidence command, section 3).
2. Each verb lands with its reader: T-047 (a), T-101 (b), T-102 (c, d), T-116 (c, d). Do not add verbs for tables no ruled task writes.

**What reads what this task adds or changes:** `emit_batch_sql.py` (through `dbcore.writable_tables`); T-047, T-101, T-102 and T-116 (the verbs); `dbcore.require_approval_heading` is read by the four new verbs, `mint-term-from-catalogue` and `add-jurisdiction`.

**Code size.** Report in the pull request the output of `git diff --shortstat "$(cat "$SCRATCH/start-commit")" -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'` (run it after `git add`, so new files count; it gives the same figure before and after the commit), and for anything added name what reads it and what existing code it replaces or makes deletable (here: the two inline approval checks the helper replaces). It counts from the commit this task started from (recorded in the set-up block), so it counts only this task's work even when the branch carries a predecessor's unmerged commits (a stacked run); `git merge-base HEAD "$BASE"` would count the predecessor's too.

## 5. Caller sweep
6:- **Owner decisions:** none. This task rests on rulings already in the ledger or on no ruling at all.

CREATE TABLE "lang_jur_map" (
    language            TEXT NOT NULL,
    jurisdiction        TEXT NOT NULL,
    role                TEXT NOT NULL
                        CHECK (role IN ('PRIMARY', 'SECONDARY')),
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT,
    created_by_session  TEXT, scope_status TEXT
    CHECK (scope_status IS NULL OR scope_status IN ('in-scope', 'scoped-out')),
    PRIMARY KEY (language, jurisdiction)
)

CREATE VIEW v_research_scope AS
-- v_research_scope: the (language, jurisdiction) pairs the research scope OWES a search for.
--
-- The ONE home of "what is owed": every lang_jur_map row not recorded `scoped-out`. A NULL scope_status is owed --
-- an unrecorded scope never shrinks the requirement (on 2026-11-06 marking four languages `scoped-out` left every
-- other row NULL, and `coverage` read required 0/0, complete true). The fill of scope_status is a data migration
-- after owner question 5; until then the requirement is the whole map, less what is recorded `scoped-out`.
-- Readers: v_coverage_priority, `db.py coverage`.
SELECT language, jurisdiction, role
  FROM lang_jur_map
 WHERE COALESCE(scope_status, 'in-scope') <> 'scoped-out'

CREATE TABLE "base_taxonomy_identity" (
  identity_code     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  display_name        TEXT NOT NULL,
  category            TEXT CHECK(category IN (
                        'mobility', 'sensory', 'cognitive', 'mental_health',
                        'pain_fatigue', 'neurological', 'developmental',
                        'general'
                      )),
  description         TEXT,
  parent_code         TEXT REFERENCES "base_taxonomy_identity"(identity_code),
  is_compound         INTEGER DEFAULT 0 CHECK(is_compound IN (0,1)),
  status              TEXT DEFAULT 'active' CHECK(status IN ('active', 'deprecated')),
  created_at          TEXT,
  updated_at          TEXT
)

CREATE TABLE base_jurisdictions (
    -- THE SHAPE OF A CODE, held by the table where a table can hold it: upper-case letters,
    -- digits and at most one dash, with a letter first; the GB prefix is the ruled rejected
    -- spelling (UK is the project's code). The dash belongs to a sub-national code and to
    -- no other kind, and a sub-national code is exactly <parent_code>-<a non-empty
    -- subdivision>. That the parent is a `country` cannot be a CHECK (it reads another
    -- row); the writer, db.py add-jurisdiction, refuses it.
    jurisdiction_code  TEXT PRIMARY KEY
                       CHECK (jurisdiction_code = UPPER(jurisdiction_code)
                              AND jurisdiction_code NOT LIKE 'GB%'
                              AND jurisdiction_code GLOB '[A-Z]*'
                              AND jurisdiction_code NOT GLOB '*[^A-Z0-9-]*'
                              AND jurisdiction_code NOT GLOB '*-*-*'
                              AND jurisdiction_code NOT GLOB '*-'),
    kind               TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('country', 'sub-national', 'meta')),
    parent_code        TEXT REFERENCES base_jurisdictions(jurisdiction_code),
    admission_ref      TEXT,
    created_at         TEXT,
    created_by_session TEXT,
    CHECK ((kind = 'sub-national') = (parent_code IS NOT NULL)),
    CHECK ((kind = 'sub-national') = (jurisdiction_code LIKE '%-%')),
    CHECK (kind <> 'sub-national'
           OR (substr(jurisdiction_code, 1, length(parent_code) + 1) = parent_code || '-'
               AND length(jurisdiction_code) > length(parent_code) + 1))
)

_OPEN_GAP = "status LIKE 'OPEN%'"


def _check_language(conn, language: str, noun: str, flag: str = "--language") -> str:
    """Refuse a language `lang_jur_map` does not hold; a new language is a doctrine change, not a
    flag. Returns the language in the map's OWN spelling, found case-insensitively (T-015), so a writer
    stores what the map holds without assuming its letter case. One home for `log-search`, `add-gap`,
    `observe-term`, `add-source --lang-detected` and `add-alias`; `noun` names the record the refusal is about
    and `flag` the option the operator typed."""
    _langs = dbcore.live_vocab(conn, "lang_jur_map", "language")
    if not _langs:
        return language
    held = {v.upper(): v for v in _langs}
    if (language or "").strip().upper() not in held:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{flag} {language!r} is not a language lang_jur_map holds "
            f"({', '.join(sorted(_langs))}). The map is the vocabulary of research "

            "(exec_id, artefact, created_by_session, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",

def _in_research_scope(language: str, jurisdiction: str = None) -> bool:
    """Does this (language, jurisdiction) pair count toward what the research scope owes?
    Reads v_research_scope, the one home of "owed"; a search with no jurisdiction names no
    pair, so it counts toward none. A sub-national jurisdiction counts toward its parent
    country (OD-04), so it is looked up as that country."""
    with connect(readonly=True) as conn:
        return bool(jurisdiction) and conn.execute(
            "SELECT 1 FROM v_research_scope WHERE language=? AND jurisdiction="
            "COALESCE((SELECT parent_code FROM base_jurisdictions WHERE jurisdiction_code=?), ?)",
            [(language or "").strip().upper(), jurisdiction, jurisdiction]).fetchone() is not None


def log_search(slug: str, language: str, query_text: str, engine: str,
               depth_method: str, session: str,
        # refuses can never be logged, so it stays owed -- hence unsearched, hence `complete`
        # stays false -- and is NAMED so the two homes' disagreement is visible (owner question 5).
        # `complete` also needs a non-empty requirement: an empty one examined nothing.
        required = [(r["language"], r["jurisdiction"]) for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT language, jurisdiction FROM v_research_scope ORDER BY 1, 2")]
        unsearched = [[r["language"], r["jurisdiction"]] for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT language, jurisdiction FROM v_coverage_priority WHERE slug=? ORDER BY 1, 2",
            [slug])]
        # SEARCHED IS READ FROM THE LOG, not taken as required-minus-unsearched: the view lists
        # unsearched pairs only for the slugs it covers, so for any other slug that subtraction
        # reads every pair searched and `complete` true over a slug nothing was logged for.
        # Same anti-join as the view (a logged row, deferred or not, names the pair).
        searched = conn.execute(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM v_research_scope v WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "
            "search_executions se LEFT JOIN base_jurisdictions b "
            "ON b.jurisdiction_code = se.jurisdiction WHERE se.slug=? "
            "AND COALESCE(b.parent_code, se.jurisdiction) = v.jurisdiction "
            "AND UPPER(se.language) = v.language)", [slug]).fetchone()["n"]
        # A search is a search whatever its spelling: the log holds `en` beside `EN`.
        outside = conn.execute(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM search_executions se LEFT JOIN base_jurisdictions b "
            "ON b.jurisdiction_code = se.jurisdiction WHERE se.slug=? "
            "AND se.deferred_reason IS NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_research_scope v "
            "WHERE v.jurisdiction = COALESCE(b.parent_code, se.jurisdiction) "
            "AND v.language = UPPER(se.language))",
            [slug]).fetchone()["n"]
        lang = conn.execute(
            "SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT UPPER(language)) AS n FROM search_executions "
            "WHERE slug=? AND deferred_reason IS NULL", [slug]).fetchone()["n"]
    unreachable = sorted({j for _, j in required if not dbcore.jurisdiction_declared(j)})
    return {
        "slug": slug,
        "pairs_required": len(required),
        "pairs_searched": searched,
        "pairs_unsearched": unsearched,
        "jurisdictions_required": len({j for _, j in required}),
        "languages_required": len({l for l, _ in required}),
        "jurisdictions_searched": jur,
        "languages_searched": lang,
        "searches_outside_scope": outside,
        "searches_deferred_with_reason": deferred,
        "jurisdictions_unreachable": unreachable,
        **({"unreachable_note": "owed by lang_jur_map, not held by base_jurisdictions: "
            "owner question 5 of the 2026-11-06 round-3 adjudication"} if unreachable else {}),
        # A slug outside ACTIVE/STUB owes nothing (R3-17): the survivor owes it. Without these
        # keys a MERGED slug read "70 pairs required, 0 searched" -- debt no search can pay.
        "slug_status": _slug["status"],
        "merged_into": _slug["merged_into"],
        **({"owes_searches": False} if _slug["status"] not in ("ACTIVE", "STUB") else {}),

## Delegated resolution 2026-11-12 — OD-21 a question about a published cell

A resolution by an Opus-class model under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-12, judged against the owner's three criteria; **not the owner's words**; standing until the owner reverses it. Reasoning and evidence: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS.md` (section OD-21).

OD-21: yes, as an open gate

**The resolution.** A reader's or the owner's objection to a published value is recorded in the database as an open gate on the cell, with who raised it and the objection's text; the cell is shown as questioned until the gate is closed by re-derivation or by a recorded answer with its warrant. The flag says "questioned", not "wrong".

**What decided it.** Criterion 1: an objection in a session file is lost provenance, and a questioned value shown unmarked overstates its standing. Criterion 2: the owner's 2026-10-30 "radically transparent for my audience". Criterion 3: objections from disabled readers about their own lens are input the book should keep.

**Reversal condition.** Gates raised faster than they can be answered, so the flag stops carrying information.

CONDITION: any session receiving an objection to a published value, or designing the cell-question gate.
ACTION: (1) Record the objection as an open gate on the cell. (2) Show the cell as questioned. (3) Close it only with a re-derivation or a recorded answer.
DATE: 2026-11-12 — delegated resolution, not an owner statement.
